overall_topic.topic: Rahul Gandhi's SIR Agitation and Protests
overall_topic.description: A televised debate analyzing Rahul Gandhi's agitation regarding voter roll irregularities (SIR), calls for the impeachment of the Chief Election Commissioner, and the broader debate on whether street protests and opposition demonstrations represent a legitimate democratic right or lead to anarchy.
key_discussion_points: Whether Rahul Gandhi's agitation is primarily about election commission integrity and constitutional questions or a political strategy.
The validity and handling of voter deletions and irregularities (SIR) across various states.
Whether political protests regarding sub-judice matters and election integrity are democratic or amount to anarchy.
The political impact of opposition protests and student demonstrations on electoral outcomes.

method.name: subtopic_to_overall_topic_embedding_alignment
method.unit_text_source: Full transcript segments within each subtopic interval; subtopic evidence is fallback only.
method.score_formula: 0.50 * cosine(unit, overall_topic+description) + 0.50 * mean(two highest cosine similarities between unit and individual key discussion points)
method.display_score: alignment_score = max(0, weighted_cosine_alignment) * 100; scaled cosine index, not a percentage or probability
method.sustained_drift_rule: Consecutive possible_drift subtopics separated by no more than 30 seconds are grouped; event duration must meet the minimum sustained duration.
method.threshold_status: provisional; manually calibrate before research claims
method.warning: Scores are heuristic semantic-alignment indicators, not probabilities or validated accuracy. Low similarity is a candidate for review, not proof of drift.

alignment_results.evidence_excerpt: Opening discussion. So let's raise the big question. Is Rahul Gandhi now going for broke with his SIR agitation? Is SIR bringing on vote-chori, bringing all anti-BJP, anti-Modi forces together? Does the SIR vote-chori issue really resonate with common citizens? is the BJP's padayatra plan to take on opposition working on the ground. Joining me now Pradeep Bhandari, the BJP's national spokesperson. Advocate Pranab Dhawan is CJP spokesperson and Gurmehar Kaur of the Congress, its spokesperson joining me. Gurmehar, let me come to you first because Rahul Gandhi in the video today says, calling all those against Amit Shah, Narendra Modi, Gyanesh Kumar to come together. So is this now about constitutional questions and the Election Commission or is this now straight a political march that targets Amit Shah and Narendra Modi as well? Sir, thank you so much for having me on your show. I actually want to start with something very simple. The BJP today has a very, very simple problem tonight. It is that it simply cannot answer the questions that are being asked by young people, so it is deciding to question patriotism instead. And what we are doing, it is Is it about the question that you're asking? Is it about the election commission, or is it about Narendra Modi and Amit Shah? Well, it is obviously about the election commission. And of course, it's linked to Modi and Shah, because they are these two people, because of whom there are these SIR irregularities that are happening. So when Rahul Gandhi says, don't worry about police or LATIs, come and save the democracy, We must go and work and save the democracy as he says. No, no. So is it about saving democracy or is it about ousting Modi Shah? Let's be clear. Has this now become less about Gyanesh Kumar and more about Modi Shah?
